Context: This story is based on the real-life account of Maud Marston, a journalist from Kearney, Nebraska. She was the only reporter to have an interview with Nellie Bly during her journey around the world.
Title: Chasing Nellie Bly
Content: Maud rushed into the house, shutting the heavy wooden door behind her. The wind whipped and the snow flurried outside, but inside it was cozy and warm with a fire blazing in the fireplace and the smell of warm bread drifting from the kitchen.
“Mama, Papa!” Maud called out as she kicked off her boots by the front door. “You are not going to believe this!”
Maud’s parents greeted her with a smile as she rounded the corner into the kitchen. “What is it, darlin’?” Papa asked, seeing the mixture of excitement and worry on his daughter’s face.
“You know that story that I have been hoping for, the `text(one)` where I will get to interview the famous Nellie Bly about her trip around the world?” she queried. “Well, I got it!”
“That is terrific news!” Mama and Papa said in unison as they reached across the table to squeeze Maud’s hand.
“But I do not understand,” Mama continued, sounding puzzled. “Why do you seem a little worried?”

“I was supposed to meet up with her train in western Nebraska,” Maud explained, “and then ride with her across the state, interviewing her as we traveled east toward Omaha. But now because of snow on the tracks, they have switched her to the Santa Fe line, so she will not be going through Nebraska at all. I will never get another chance like this. Never!”
Papa smiled and winked at Maud. “Now if I know my `ultext(headstrong)` daughter, she is not going to let a little detail like that get in her way. You will think of something; I am sure of it!”

That night, Maud tossed and turned in her bed, her mind spinning with wild nightmares about a journalism career in ruins. She tried to calm her thoughts and think about pleasant things. She `ultext(mused)` about nature and the beauty of the `text(Earth)` to forget about her troubles. But as soon as that topic entered her mind, she pictured the snow piling high on the tracks and blocking Nellie’s path to Nebraska.

At some point during the night, Maud must have drifted off to sleep because the next thing she knew, she was waking up in her warm bed to the aroma of hotcakes and bacon drifting from the kitchen. The smell immediately made her think of the time she and Papa went to Kansas City together for `text(one)` of his business trips. She could still taste those delicious hotcakes dripping with syrup and that crunchy bacon and . . .
Suddenly Maud sprang out of bed, pulling her robe and slippers on as quickly as possible. She had the idea of a lifetime!
“Papa, Mama,” Maud called as she darted down the stairs in the old farmhouse, “you are not going to believe what that smell of bacon and hotcakes just inspired me to realize!”
Papa and Mama laughed at Maud’s excitement and her slightly disheveled appearance. “What is it, Maud? We are on pins and needles waiting!” Mama said, giving her daughter a good-morning hug.
“Nellie’s train goes right through Kansas City. I could take the train from here to Omaha and transfer down to Kansas City and meet up with her!”
“That is a brilliant idea!” Papa replied. “But how did the smell of hotcakes and bacon cause you to think of that?” he asked, curious.

“Thanks to you, Papa, and that business trip breakfast I ate with you in Kansas City years ago, the idea just flowed into my brain along with that smell of sizzling bacon!” Maud explained. “If you are up for a return trip, I would love it if you rode with me to Kansas City!”

“Well, if you `text(two)` are going to make this morning’s train, you should get a move on!” Mama prodded them along, knowing that Maud still had to gather her things and make herself presentable before she left. “And in honor of its memory-boosting power, I will wrap up some bacon-rolled hotcakes for you to eat on the road!”
